cards.text: Last time, Solomon finished the house of the LORD in seven years (1 Kings 6:38). Now he turns to his own house: his palace. And friend, this is NOT a weekend project.

cards.question: How long does it take Solomon to complete his entire palace?

cards.text: Then the building plans roll out: the House of the Forest of Lebanon with rows of cedar pillars, a colonnade, the Hall of Justice where Solomon will judge, his own palace, and a palace like that hall for Pharaoh's daughter, whom he had married. All of it is built with cedar and big, costly stones.
Now King Solomon sends for a craftsman named Huram. Me? I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, and the only one anybody ever came for was the scissors.

cards.question: King Solomon sends to bring Huram from ___.

cards.text: Huram's mother is a widow from the tribe of Naphtali. His father was a man of Tyre.

cards.question: Huram has great skill, understanding and knowledge for every kind of ___ work.
Like Huram, his father was a craftsman in bronze.
Huram comes to King Solomon but goes home before the work is done.

cards.text: Then Huram goes to work, and it's ALL bronze: two tall pillars at the temple's portico named Jachin and Boaz, and a huge round basin called the Sea resting on twelve bronze oxen. He also makes ten stands on wheels with a basin for each, plus pots, shovels and sprinkling bowls.

cards.question: Where does the king have Huram's bronze pieces cast in clay molds?

answers.text: In the plain of the Jordan

cards.text: And get this. Solomon never weighs any of it. Me? I came with a price sticker. Twenty-five cents.

cards.question: Why does Solomon leave all of Huram's bronze pieces unweighed?

answers.text: There were so many of them
The bronze was a gift from Tyre

cards.text: Solomon also makes the furnishings for the house of the LORD, and these are GOLD. The golden altar, the golden table for the Bread of the Presence, ten lampstands of pure gold, lamps, basins, right down to gold hinges on the doors.

cards.question: All the work for the house of the LORD is completed. Then Solomon brings in silver, gold and furnishings. Who had dedicated them?
Solomon places David's silver, gold and furnishings in the ___ of the house of the LORD.

cards.text: But friend, don't take your apron off yet. This story is not done.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences when "Me?" is counted, exceeding the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Calling Huram a craftsman draws on his bronze skill and work in 1 Kings 7:14, but the card cites only 7:13, which says that Solomon sent to bring him from Tyre.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker infer Tyre. The blank therefore asks for an unseen word rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The earlier cards call Huram a craftsman and identify his parents, but give no basis for inferring that his work is bronze. Choosing bronze, stone or cedar is consequently an unsupported guess at unseen wording.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card is punctuated as five sentences, including "Me?" and "Twenty-five cents.", well beyond the two-sentence limit for a non-opening story card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Most of the stop's choices are not informed guesses. Cards 2, 5, 7, 8, 11 and 15 require facts that the earlier cards give no basis for reasoning out, and card 9 is likewise an unsupported true-or-false prediction. Only cards 13 and 16 clearly provide a reasoning basis, so discovery questions make up most of the stop rather than a few exceptions.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
